channel.title: MIA — Management Intelligence Alert
channel.description: daily selected and enriched macroeconomic and political news

item.title: Trump called a Ukraine deal "closer than many think" ahead of the Ankara NATO summit, while the UK sanctioned Russian chemical-weapons institutes, nearly all of Russia's 83 regions faced fuel shortages, and Macron opened a new Syria channel.
item.description:
The 7-8 July NATO summit in Ankara centres on Ukraine: Trump spoke separately with Putin and Zelensky, plans to meet Zelensky Wednesday, and expects to follow up with Putin afterward. A draft Ankara Declaration reportedly includes €70 billion for Ukraine, though Italy is blocking parts of the commitment, even as all 32 allies now meet 2% GDP defence spending. Diplomacy proceeds against a backdrop of pressure on Moscow: the UK sanctioned two Russian institutes and seven individuals linked to the Novichok poisonings of Sergei Skripal and Alexei Navalny, mirroring an earlier EU move, while a CNN analysis found nearly all of Russia's 83 regions rationing fuel after sustained Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries. Separately, Macron became the first major Western leader to visit Syria since Assad's fall, ahead of a possible Trump-al-Sharaa meeting in Ankara.

Industry Impact

For the chemical and ACS industry, a credible ceasefire would eventually unlock large European reconstruction demand and ease energy prices, while continued Russian fuel disruption keeps regional feedstock and logistics risk elevated. Benchmarked against the June diplomatic opening covered on 5 July, this week adds concrete summit deliverables and tightening pressure on Russia — a more actionable, but still unresolved, situation.

Chinatimes | Süddeutsche Zeitung | MarketScreener | The Times of India | Arab News | NPR

item.title: The IEA says the world absorbed the loss of over a billion barrels of oil since the Iran war began, and prices are back near pre-war levels — but drained reserves and an unresolved conflict leave the market exposed to fresh spikes.
item.description:
Reuters reports the Iran war produced the largest oil supply disruption in history by volume, yet it was absorbed with surprising ease as OPEC+ raised output and Gulf shipping through Hormuz recovered; Saudi Arabia's biggest-ever monthly price cut to Asian buyers confirms the return to normal trading. China weathered the shock through accumulated reserves and sharply reduced imports, while a UAE shipping operator used opaque "dark" tanker transits through Hormuz to keep exports flowing at a profit. Bloomberg Economics nonetheless expects global interest rates to stay elevated by up to half a percentage point through 2028, citing lingering inflation risk from the energy shock and the AI investment boom.

Industry Impact

For chemical and ACS producers, naphtha and crude remain the primary cost anchors for resins, polymers and solvents; the price normalisation supports the margin-relief thesis flagged in Ifo's June sentiment rebound (see insight 3). The IEA's own caution — that buffer stocks are now thin and a durable peace is not secured — is the key risk: any renewed disruption would hit a market with far less spare capacity than in February. Benchmarked against the acute-shock phase, the situation has shifted from crisis to fragile normalisation.

Reuters | The Straits Times | Business Recorder | Cinco Días | The Economic Times | The Economic Times — UAE Shipping

item.title: German industrial orders rose 1.9% in May, beating forecasts, while US job growth held at 57,000 and services PMI eased to 54.0. The ESM warned a combined US asset sell-off and Middle East shock could tip the euro area into recession; China reported 5.4% average annual growth over five years.
item.description:
Germany's Destatis data show May order intake up 1.9% against a roughly 1% consensus, though this only partly reverses April's revised 3.2% drop — a tentative, order-driven upswing rather than a broad recovery. In the US, unemployment held at 4.2% on 57,000 new jobs and 3.5% wage growth, while the ISM non-manufacturing PMI slipped to 54.0 as front-loaded orders from the Middle East war faded; the dollar sits near a two-week low on reduced Fed hike bets. The ESM's first annual Euro Area Stability Watch report is the sharper warning: eurozone exposure to US markets has risen to 47% of GDP from 18% in 2013, and a simultaneous US equity correction and new Middle East conflict could send European shares down nearly 30% over 18 months and push euro-area growth to just 0.6% in 2026 before a 0.4% contraction in 2027. China, meanwhile, reported 5.4% average annual growth over the past five years and per-capita GDP above USD 13,000.

Industry Impact

For Henkel, the German order uptick is an encouraging demand signal for industrial adhesives, but the ESM's tail-risk scenario — a US-market shock compounding any Middle East relapse — is the more consequential number: it would hit European construction and industrial demand harder and faster than the current data suggests. Benchmarked against the 5 July Ifo sentiment rebound, direction is still positive but fragility is rising, not falling.

Süddeutsche Zeitung | Handelsblatt | MarketScreener | The Economic Times | Reuters — ESM | People's Daily Online

item.title: An ICC/KPMG report says chemical supply chains face a "decade of uncertainty" from geopolitical fragmentation and feedstock volatility, just as an EEB/Corporate Europe Observatory investigation accuses the industry-dominated EU Critical Chemicals Alliance of shaping Brussels' competitiveness agenda in its own favour.
item.description:
KPMG's "Beyond the Horizon" white paper, presented at ICC's LogNext 2026 conference in Mumbai, argues that supply chain models built around scale and efficiency are being outpaced by geopolitical fragmentation, maritime chokepoint risk, climate disruption, feedstock volatility and regulatory divergence — future competitiveness will depend on early-warning capability and adaptability rather than pure cost optimisation. On the same day, Corporate Europe Observatory and the EEB published "Captured! The Critical Chemicals Alliance: by industry, for industry," finding that of the Alliance's 293 members, industry (companies and trade associations, led by Cefic) accounts for 72% versus 4.4% civil society — a 16-to-1 imbalance — and arguing the Commission has let incumbents including BASF and TotalEnergies define what counts as "critical" for future state aid and industrial policy.

Industry Impact

The two reports frame opposite sides of the same story: the industry's own diagnosis of external uncertainty, and an external diagnosis of the industry's influence over how the EU responds to it. For ACS producers, the practical stakes are which chemicals and sites get labelled "critical" — a designation likely to steer state aid, energy-cost relief and permitting priority. Benchmarked against past EU sectoral alliances, unusually skewed membership raises the risk of a credibility challenge to whatever the Alliance ultimately recommends.

Indian Chemical Council / KPMG | Euronews | Corporate Europe Observatory

item.title: China's antimony export licensing — controlling up to 90% of global refining — is deepening uncertainty for European chemical and defence firms; exports fell roughly 97% after 2024 controls tightened and prices have nearly tripled, pushing buyers toward new mines outside China.
item.description:
Wallstreet:online reports that European chemical and defence companies, including names linked to Hensoldt and BASF supply chains, face a critical bottleneck in antimony — used in flame retardants, batteries and munitions such as armour-piercing rounds and infrared optics. Independent research confirms the scale of the disruption: China's August 2024 restrictions and a whitelist limiting exports to eleven approved companies through 2026-27 cut shipments by around 97% and roughly tripled global prices, with the JRC noting that licence reviews now routinely exceed 45 days, shifting the risk from outright denial to slow-walking approvals. Europe's broader rearmament and clean-tech ambitions compound the exposure, since antimony sits alongside gallium, tungsten and graphite on the list of Chinese-controlled inputs critical to defence and electronics.

Industry Impact

This is a direct feedstock and cost risk for the chemical industry's flame-retardant and specialty-additive segments, and a slower-moving structural risk for defence-linked coatings and composites. The response mirrors the rare-earth playbook seen with the EU-China talks in early July: diversify sourcing to non-Chinese jurisdictions now, since new mine capacity takes years to permit. Benchmarked against rare earths, antimony is a smaller market but arguably more acute, given the near-total concentration of refining capacity in China.

Wallstreet:online | JRC — European Commission | CSIS

item.title: The Paris Court of Appeal ruled on Marine Le Pen's five-year ineligibility ban on 7 July; if upheld, her presidential ambitions end and Jordan Bardella becomes National Rally's likely candidate, while centrist hopefuls pitch growth-friendly budget restraint to block a far-right win.
item.description:
Le Pen was convicted in 2025 of embezzling European Parliament funds and faces a ban that would exclude her from the April-May 2027 election unless the court reduces her ineligibility to two years or less. Bardella, her chosen successor, stands ready if she is barred, and polls make the National Rally's eventual nominee the strong favourite for the run-off. Against this backdrop, centrist figures including Édouard Philippe are positioning as the establishment's answer, pledging to tame public finances without choking growth — a deliberate contrast with both the far-right and hard-left, where Jean-Luc Mélenchon could also feature.

Industry Impact

For the chemical and ACS industry, France's political trajectory matters mainly through fiscal and euro-area stability: a National Rally-led government would likely challenge EU fiscal rules and trade positioning, while a centrist outcome preserves continuity. Combined with Christine Lagarde's own possible entry into the race (flagged 5 July), French political risk over the next nine months is rising in parallel with the ECB leadership question. Benchmarked against 2022 and the earlier legislative elections, judicial rulings — not just polling — are now a first-order variable in French political risk.

Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung | MarketScreener | Euronews | France 24

item.title: Andy Burnham, the only declared candidate to succeed Keir Starmer, is on track to become Labour leader on 17 July and prime minister on 20 July. He has ruled out a snap election and pledged to govern on Labour's existing 2024 manifesto.
item.description:
Burnham's uncontested path to Downing Street removes near-term political uncertainty for the UK, since he has committed to the current policy platform rather than a fresh mandate. This continuity signal matters for investment planning: no early election means no near-term reset of tax, trade or industrial policy, at least through the remainder of this parliament. It follows the same week the UK deepened Russia sanctions and continues to prepare its 2027 carbon border tax and chemical-sector emissions rules flagged on 5 July, none of which a leadership change is likely to alter.

Industry Impact

For chemical and ACS producers with UK operations, the practical takeaway is regulatory stability over the next 12-18 months: existing CBAM, BAT emissions and industrial-strategy timelines should proceed unchanged. Benchmarked against Rishi Sunak's and Liz Truss's earlier leadership transitions, an uncontested, manifesto-continuity succession is a markedly lower-risk pattern, reducing (rather than adding to) UK political-risk premium in the near term.

Lianhe Zaobao

item.title: Morgan Stanley projects the global robotaxi market will reach USD 1 trillion by 2040, with Chinese-made hardware costs falling to USD 35,000-40,000 per vehicle by 2027 and fleets covering their own operating costs by 2028, positioning Baidu, Xpeng and WeRide alongside Tesla and Waymo.
item.description:
The bank frames falling Chinese manufacturing costs as a "major underappreciated accelerant" for the sector: cheaper supply chains, advancing AI and clearer regulation are expected to let robotaxi operators break even on vehicle operating costs by 2028, setting up scaled commercial deployment around 2030. Chinese players are positioned as regional front-runners on cost, competing with Tesla and Waymo's more established but pricier platforms.

Industry Impact

For the ACS industry, large-scale robotaxi and broader autonomous-fleet rollout is a demand driver for structural and thermal-interface adhesives, sensor-housing sealants and specialty coatings used in sensor pods, battery packs and lightweight body panels — an extension of the electronics-and-EV materials story already visible in China's EV export boom (see insight 10). The read-through is similar to GCAP's aerospace materials case flagged on 5 July: near-term revenue is limited, but early qualification with Chinese and US robotaxi platforms secures a position in a market this bank expects to scale meaningfully by 2030. Benchmarked against the current robotaxi base (still small commercial fleets), the 2030 breakeven point is the milestone to track, not the 2040 headline figure.

South China Morning Post

item.title: China's industrial robot exports rose 48.7% in 2025 and a further 39.5% in January-May 2026 to 86,597 units, while total robot exports (including cleaning and bionic robots) reached 10.4 million units worth CNY 20 billion, sold to over 150 countries.
item.description:
Customs data show China's industrial robot exports first exceeded imports in 2025, and monthly volumes now regularly top 20,000-25,000 units, up nearly 90% year-on-year in April 2026 alone. The broader robotics category is even larger by value: cleaning robots account for over 70% of the CNY 20 billion in January-May export value, alongside roughly 70,000 industrial units and more than 8,000 intelligent bionic robots, with ASEAN and the EU as the largest destination markets.

Industry Impact

This scale-up is directly relevant to ACS producers as a materials-demand driver: industrial and service robots require structural and vibration-damping adhesives, precision-bonded sensor and actuator assemblies, and protective coatings for outdoor and industrial-duty units. The export mix — weighted toward lower-cost cleaning robots but growing fastest in industrial and bionic categories — suggests China is moving up the robotics value chain, mirroring the trajectory already seen in EVs (insight 10) and batteries. Benchmarked against China's electric-vehicle export ramp of the past three years, robotics exports are following a similar compounding growth curve roughly two to three years behind, implying a comparable materials-demand inflection is still ahead rather than behind.

China Economic Net | Commercial Times

item.title: BYD overtook Tesla in global EV sales despite an 8.2% delivery decline, and Chery, BYD and Geely posted 79.7%, ~100% and 157% export growth in June; Chinese brands hit a record 12% share of new European registrations even as domestic industry profits fell 20% on price competition.
item.description:
BYD's 557,090 deliveries in April-June, though down year-on-year, were enough to reclaim the global EV sales lead from Tesla on the strength of overseas shipments. Export growth is now the industry's dominant engine: Chery's exports rose 79.7% to 191,062 units and accounted for nearly 80% of its June sales, while Geely's overseas shipments surged 157%. In Europe, Chinese brands reached a record 12% share of new registrations across 32 countries in May, overtaking Japanese brands (11.3%) for the first time — consistent with the 10% western-European share already flagged for April. At home, the China Passenger Car Association reports industry profits fell 20% to CNY 144 billion in January-May, with margins at a five-year low of 3.4% amid an intense domestic price war and a 19% drop in retail volumes.

Industry Impact

For Henkel and other ACS suppliers, the pattern is a widening gap between a highly profitable export channel and a margin-compressed domestic market — automakers are likely to push harder on cost in domestic sourcing while competing on speed and localisation abroad. Benchmarked against the European share data covered on 5 July, the trend has accelerated further within a single month, reinforcing that supplier qualification speed, not just price, will decide market position.

South China Morning Post | China Daily — Exports | China Daily — Profits | Commercial Times

item.title: Germany's commercial and residential property investment reached €16.6 billion in H1 2026, up 20%, its strongest first half in years; Italy's market rose 28% to €7 billion, 62% above its ten-year average, led by retail and logistics.
item.description:
Cushman & Wakefield's data show Germany's H1 volume split between €12.7 billion in commercial deals (up 25%) and a resilient residential segment, marking a clear recovery from the post-2022 rate-driven downturn. Italy's Dils research shows an even sharper rebound, with retail (€2.3 billion) and logistics (nearly €1.2 billion, a four-year high) leading, and office investment up 13% concentrated in Milan and Rome.

Industry Impact

Real estate investment volumes are a leading indicator for construction activity 12-18 months out, making this a relevant early signal for adhesives, sealants and coatings demand tied to renovation and new-build cycles in Germany and Italy specifically. Combined with the German industrial-order uptick (insight 3) and the Ifo chemical-sentiment rebound flagged on 5 July, this adds a third, independent data point pointing toward a gradual German and southern-European demand recovery. Benchmarked against the trough years of 2023-2024, both markets remain well below their 2021 peaks, so this is a rebound in the pace of decline reversing, not yet a return to prior investment levels.

MarketScreener | Il Sole 24 Ore

item.title: India expects to finish legal scrubbing of its EU free-trade agreement within three weeks, targeting signature by end-2026, even as ASEAN presses New Delhi for deeper tariff cuts to narrow a trade deficit that has widened to USD 45.2 billion from USD 7 billion in 2010.
item.description:
Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the India-EU pact, which would give Indian exporters access to 27 developed EU economies, should be signed by end-2026 and implemented in Q1 2027; he travels to Spain, Belgium and Finland later this month to prepare implementation. In parallel, ASEAN is pushing India for greater tariff concessions in the ongoing review of the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement, as its trade surplus with India has widened sharply since the pact took effect in 2010.

Industry Impact

For the chemical and ACS industry, a completed EU-India FTA would improve market access and potentially tariff treatment for European chemical exports into a fast-growing manufacturing base, complementing India's own construction and automotive growth. The ASEAN review cuts the other way, signalling India may face pressure to open further to Asian competition, including chemical and intermediate goods, as a condition of narrowing its own deficit. Benchmarked against the EU-China trade reset covered on 5 July, India is pursuing deeper integration with the EU precisely as the EU's relationship with China stays adversarial — a diversification opportunity for supply chains looking beyond China.

The Economic Times — India-EU | The Hindu Business Line — ASEAN

item.title: CIPS's Q2 2026 Pulse Survey shows procurement professionals still rate the risk environment historically high, with short-term disruption concern easing to 4.95 from a Q1 peak of 5.69 on a 1-7 scale, but above any reading of the prior two and a half years bar that peak.
item.description:
The survey confirms what this week's oil and Russia coverage implies quantitatively: the Middle East conflict, the broader geopolitical climate and the Ukraine war remain the dominant concerns for procurement and supply chain professionals globally, even as the most acute phase of the Iran war has passed. The modest sequential improvement from Q1's peak tracks the oil-market normalisation covered in insight 2, but the level remains well above the two-and-a-half-year baseline, indicating professionals are not yet treating the de-escalation as durable.

Industry Impact

For Henkel's own procurement and supply chain functions, this is a useful external benchmark: peer organisations are still operating in a heightened-risk posture despite improving headline indicators, which argues against relaxing dual-sourcing and buffer-stock practices adopted during the acute crisis phase. Benchmarked against the Q1 2026 peak, this quarter's reading is the first sequential improvement in the current cycle, a tentative but real turning point worth monitoring into Q3.

CIPS
